required.D1_exit_reason_record: Diagnostic presence rule, never an upgrade: for every application attempt the manager reaped, the decoded session records contain exactly one exit_reason line in session-result.txt (attempt=N exit_reason=full|basic|query_failed errno=E) and one event=ExitReason journal line in manager-status.log, with payload at most 320 bytes. A reaped attempt with exit_reason=not_observed fails D1. The recorded namespace, code, flags and payload are reported as observed kernel facts; any sender pid or process name is attributed only from the decoded kcdata payload. D1 passing never satisfies or excuses any C1-C9 failure, and a SIGKILL or nonzero application wait stays a failure.
required.D2_code_signing_flags_record: Diagnostic presence rule, never an upgrade: for every application attempt with an owned PID, the decoded session-result.txt has exactly one line attempt=N cs_at_spawn=flags=0x........|query_failed errno=E cs_at_exit=...; cs_at_spawn=not_observed fails D2. For a reaped attempt whose exit_reason is recorded, cs_at_exit is flags or query_failed (ESRCH is acceptable and reported as such). manager-status.log has one scope=manager self_cs_status line. Recorded flags are reported as observed kernel facts (CS_VALID 0x1, CS_HARD 0x100, CS_KILL 0x200, CS_KILLED 0x1000000 etc. per pinned sys/codesign.h); a kill-path interpretation must cite them, never assume them.
required.D3_serialized_launch_observed: Behaviour-validity rule, never an upgrade: if a second application attempt exists, its SpawnReturned observed_ms is greater than or equal to the first attempt's AppReady observed_ms (or the first attempt's AppReaped observed_ms if it never became READY). A second attempt spawned before either fails D3, and then no concurrency conclusion may be drawn. If the first attempt fails before READY and no second attempt exists, D3 is reported as not_applicable and C2/C3 still fail for the missing launch.
required.D4_kernel_message_record: Diagnostic presence rule, never an upgrade: for every application attempt reaped with a signal wait status, the decoded session-result.txt has exactly one line attempt=N kernel_messages=read euid=E bytes=B matched=M kept=K | query_failed euid=E errno=E | unsupported, followed by exactly K lines attempt=N kernel_message[i]=TEXT for i=0..K-1; kernel_messages=not_observed for such an attempt fails D4. manager-status.log has one event=KernelMessages line for that attempt and K event=KernelMessage lines whose text matches the snapshot lines in order. An attempt reaped with a normal exit shows kernel_messages=not_observed. Kept lines are reported verbatim as observed kernel log text. The resource-limit fatal-port mechanism may be called confirmed for an attempt only if a kept line contains "caught allocating too many" and names that attempt's process and PID as chonk-terminal-d[PID]. A read as euid 0 with matched=0 counts against the mechanism for that attempt; query_failed or unsupported leaves it untested. D4 never satisfies or excuses any C1-C9 failure, and a SIGKILL stays a failure.
required.D5_fix_attribution: Interpretation rule fixed before boot, never an upgrade: C1-C9 alone decide qualification. A passing closed lifecycle may be attributed to the libSystem spawn-attribute fix only because candidate-005 differs from candidate-004 in that one member; it is reported as the fix being effective in this run, not as proof for every spawner. If any application is still reaped by a signal, its D4 lines decide the reading: a kept "caught allocating too many" line naming that process means resource limits still reach it and the fix is not effective for that path; matched=0 as euid 0 means a different cause. Any other new failure (for example a system process misbehaving after the libSystem change) is recorded as a regression of this candidate and is not hidden by C-results of individual apps.
